title: Greenpeace protesters disrupt Nvidia CEO keynote in Berlin

tea.why: Protesters interrupted an Nvidia CEO keynote in Berlin to challenge the company over environmental destruction and military chip usage.
tea.want: Protesters demanded answers regarding Nvidia chips allegedly found in Russian drones and broader environmental concerns.
tea.changed: Oct 21, 2026: Greenpeace activists interrupted Jensen Huang's GTC keynote in Berlin before being escorted out by security.

summary: On October 21, 2026, Greenpeace activists disrupted the Nvidia GTC keynote address delivered by CEO Jensen Huang at the Tempodrom in Berlin. Standing on chairs with a banner bearing the Greenpeace logo and the slogan "Nvidia, clean up your dirty business!", the protesters challenged the CEO regarding the alleged presence of Nvidia chips in Russian drones and raised broader concerns about environmental destruction. As security guards quickly intervened to remove the individuals from the premises, Huang responded by telling them to go easy and stating he would talk to them later, before resuming his presentation.
demands: Clean up dirty business and environmental destruction
Explain technology found in Russian drones
response: Security personnel rushed to escort the protesters out of the hall. CEO Jensen Huang responded on stage by stating, "It's okay, go easy," and "I'll talk to you later," before continuing his keynote address.

updates.text: Greenpeace protesters interrupted Jensen Huang's Nvidia GTC keynote in Berlin to demand answers over chips in Russian drones.
